style: natural spoken dubbing, concise but faithful

segments.text: Welcome back to LingoWave.
Today we are testing a real media-processing pipeline.
The API stores the upload in S3 and sends a job to SQS.
A CPU worker then downloads the asset and transcribes the speech.
Keep the product name LingoWave exactly as written.
The build completed in 18.196 seconds on a four-vCPU worker.
Do not translate the URL https://example.com or the number 42.
This phrase is intentionally idiomatic: the ball is in your court.
The speaker sounds calm, precise, and helpful.
A shorter line is better than a literal and awkward sentence.
Preserve names such as Dr. Ada Lovelace and Istanbul.
The target audio should fit the original timing window.
If a line is too long, rewrite it once before speed adjustment.
Never add commentary such as here is your translation.
The AWS Translate adapter is optional and must not block this path.
The pending GPU quota request remains open for a later upgrade.
CPU validation should still produce a downloadable MP4.
Measure wall time, memory, CPU usage, and cost per minute.
This is a technical benchmark, not a customer-facing script.
Finally, release temporary compute and report every remaining blocker.
